q-31655.name: Question 2
q-31655.worked_solution:
A rule is a function if and only if every input is mapped to *precisely one* output.

- If we substitute the $xy$-pair $(3,2)$ into our table, we get a function.

| **$x$** | $-6$ | $-3$ | $-1$ | $3$ | $4$ | $7$ | $9$ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $y$ | $30$ | $26$ | $1$ | $2$ | $3$ | $12$ | $28$ |

Notice that all values in the first row are *distinct* (i.e., different). Every input value is assigned to *precisely one* output value.

- None of the other $xy$-pairs gives rules that are functions. So, for example, substituting the $xy$-pair $(4,12)$ gives a rule that is *not* a function. 

| **$x$** | $-6$ | $-3$ | $-1$ | $4$ | $4$ | $7$ | $9$ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $y$ | $30$ | $26$ | $1$ | $12$ | $3$ | $12$ | $28$ |

Notice that the first row contains the value $x=4$ twice. The input value $4$ is assigned to *more than one* output value ($3$ and $12$).

q-31655.html:
Question 2
?

Which missing xy-pair would make the following rule a function?

x −6 −3 −1 ? 4 7 9
y 30 26 1 ? 3 12 28
a
(−1,28)
b
(3,2)
c
(4,12)
d
(9,26)
e
(−6,1)
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

A rule is a function if and only if every input is mapped to precisely one output.

  • If we substitute the xy-pair (3,2) into our table, we get a function.

    x −6 −3 −1 3 4 7 9
    y 30 26 1 2 3 12 28

    Notice that all values in the first row are distinct (i.e., different). Every input value is assigned to precisely one output value.

  • None of the other xy-pairs gives rules that are functions. So, for example, substituting the xy-pair (4,12) gives a rule that is not a function.

    x −6 −3 −1 4 4 7 9
    y 30 26 1 12 3 12 28

    Notice that the first row contains the value x=4 twice. The input value 4 is assigned to more than one output value (3 and 12).
